blocks.text: The docstring describes the two distinct audiences this single router serves: the terminal (no session, /v1/code/devices/*) and the signed-in web app (/api/devices/*). It lists all routes for both audiences. The imports include Pydantic SecretStr and the eo/devices domain module.
blocks.title: Module docstring, imports and audience overview

blocks.text: PairStartRequest holds device_name (sanitised by _plain_label), os, and client_version. _plain_label is a Pydantic field validator that strips dangerous characters. PairStartResponse carries the codes the terminal must display to the user.
blocks.title: Request and response models for the terminal pairing flow

blocks.text: DeviceOut is the wire shape for one device in the web-app list. _http_error translates DeviceError subclasses to fixed HTTP status codes and messages that never echo input — a deliberate security choice preventing information leakage about which part of the request was wrong.
blocks.title: DeviceOut and _http_error: the response model and error mapper

blocks.text: pair_start initiates a pairing, pair_poll lets the terminal check status, and device_token exchanges an approved code for a credential. All three set Cache-Control: no-store on responses that carry secrets or codes. Errors go through _http_error.
blocks.title: Terminal-facing pairing routes (no auth required)

blocks.text: approve_device and deny_device are called by the signed-in user in the web app. They require require_auth and act on a user_code — the human-readable code the terminal showed on screen. Both delegate to eo/devices and pass errors through _http_error.
blocks.title: Web-app routes: approve and deny

blocks.text: list_my_devices returns paired devices for the authenticated account; include_revoked=True adds already-revoked ones. revoke_my_device deletes a specific device's access, invalidating its token via eo/devices.
blocks.title: Web-app routes: list and revoke devices

how_it_works: One router is mounted with a single include_router call in api/server.py.
Terminal routes (/v1/code/devices/*) have no session requirement.

_http_error() maps DeviceError subclasses to specific HTTP status codes (429 RateLimitError, 503 ServiceUnavailable, 404 NotFound, 400 BadRequest, 401 Unauthorized) with fixed error messages that never echo input.
Secrets arrive as Pydantic SecretStr and responses that expose them set Cache-Control: no-store.
purpose: Implements the HTTP surface for the OAuth-device-flow-style pairing that lets a terminal (m2c login) become a trusted device without a browser session. Secrets are held as Pydantic SecretStr and responses that carry them are marked Cache-Control: no-store.
summary: FastAPI router for M2C device-pairing (S03): two audiences (terminal and web app) under /v1/code/devices/* and /api/devices/*, with secret handling and fixed error messages.
